Note::keep_ascii¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::keep_ascii() const

Drop Every Non-ASCII Byte From Every Cell¶

keep_ascii() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every byte >= 0x80 deleted from each cell. What remains is exactly the ASCII content — letters, digits, whitespace, punctuation, and ASCII control bytes are all kept; accented letters, non-Latin scripts, and emoji are removed.

This is a lossy coercion, not a transliteration: "café" becomes "caf", not "cafe". When you want accented letters folded to their base ASCII forms, use transliterate_ascii() (or to_ascii()) instead; use keep_ascii() only when non-ASCII content is genuinely unwanted.

keep_ascii is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"café résumé", "plain", "日本語 text"}).keep_ascii())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["caf rsum", "plain", " text"]

The accented letters and the CJK characters are dropped; the ASCII spaces between them stay.

See Also¶

  • pluss::coden::Note::transliterate_ascii: fold non-ASCII to ASCII equivalents instead of deleting them.

  • Note::is_ascii: test whether a cell is already pure ASCII.

  • Note::keep_printable: also drop ASCII control bytes.

  • Note::remove_emojis: drop only emoji, keep other non-ASCII text.
